tldr: "Control plane" surfaced as a shared label for three unrelated projects this month: an arXiv paper proposing a governance layer for enterprise AI systems, a solo developer's Show HN tool for orchestrating coding agents, and AWS's shipped Claude apps gateway. The items share a phrase, not a storyline — each is a standalone read.
whats_new: The newest item is AWS's Claude apps gateway (also its own launch thread), which explicitly brands itself a "self-hosted control plane" for identity, policy, telemetry, routing, and spend caps.
why_it_matters: "Control plane" means three different things here: an academic governance-layer design, a single-developer MCP orchestrator, and a shipped, supported deployment gateway — only the last one is something you can deploy today.

status.detail: Three unrelated teams converged on "control plane" language this month; only AWS's Claude apps gateway is a shipped product.

beats.headline: AGL-1 paper proposes a governance layer as an enterprise AI control plane
beats.summary: Academic design for a trust layer across copilots, RAG systems, and autonomous agents — a proposal, not a shipped system.

beats.headline: Show HN: PlanWright pitches itself as a control plane for AI coding agents
beats.summary: An MCP-driven tool for planning in Claude Desktop, implementing in Codex, and reviewing in a custom triage agent, with decisions logged across each hop.

beats.headline: AWS brands its Claude apps gateway a self-hosted control plane
beats.summary: The only shipped, supported entry in this cluster: centralized identity, policy, telemetry, routing, and spend caps for Claude Code and Claude Desktop.

open_questions: Does AGL-1's governance-layer design get adopted or benchmarked by a real enterprise deployment?
Does PlanWright gain contributors or usage beyond the initial Show HN post?
Do more vendors converge on "control plane" language for agent or LLM deployment management?
take_for_builders: Don't treat these as one trend to track — if you need agent governance today, evaluate AWS's shipped Claude apps gateway; treat AGL-1 and PlanWright as an early research idea and a single-developer tool, not production options.
